title: Revised PARF rebate: impact on car prices, demand and COE renewals
asked: Whether studies were done on how the revised Preferential Additional Registration Fee (PARF) rebate schedule affects car depreciation rates, new car demand and COE renewal behaviour, and whether the findings can be shared; whether transitional measures were considered for buyers who planned purchases under the previous depreciation framework; and how the revision affects new car prices and what recourse exists for buyers who bought cars but have not registered their COEs before 6 February 2026.
asked_by: Mr Victor Lye and Ms Poh Li San
response: The PARF rebate was lowered and the rebate cap cut from $60,000 to $30,000 because EVs are now more common, which makes encouraging early deregistration less necessary. The changes took immediate effect to avoid bidders rushing to market or distorting the COE market, and vehicle taxes and rebates are levied at the point of registration, not the point of sale. Fewer than 2,000 car buyers with committed purchases are estimated to be affected, mostly buyers of higher-end internal combustion engine cars, and buyers who have yet to secure a COE may wish to discuss with their dealers.

key_points.point: The PARF rebate was lowered and the rebate cap reduced from $60,000 to $30,000.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: This is why we lowered the PARF rebate and also reduced the rebate cap from $60,000 to $30,000.

key_points.point: The ministry does not expect the changes to significantly affect COE renewal behaviour.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: We do not expect the changes to affect Certificate of Entitlement (COE) renewal behaviour significantly.

key_points.point: The changes were implemented with immediate effect to avoid bidders rushing to market or distorting the COE market.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: The recent changes to vehicle taxes were implemented with immediate effect, in line with our general approach on market sensitive tax changes.

key_points.point: Vehicle taxes and rebates are levied at the point of registration, not the point of sale, so buyers in a COE bidding exercise are treated equally.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: Vehicle taxes and rebates are also consistently levied at the point of registration, not the point of sale

key_points.point: Fewer than 2,000 car buyers with committed purchases are estimated to be affected, mostly buyers of higher-end internal combustion engine cars.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: Fewer than 2,000 car buyers with committed purchases are estimated to be affected.

key_points.point: Buyers with existing purchase agreements who have not yet secured a COE may wish to discuss with their dealers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: Buyers with existing purchase agreements who have yet to secure a COE may wish to discuss with their dealers to come to a mutually acceptable agreement.

key_points.point: Some dealers have already made alternative arrangements with affected buyers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: We understand that some dealers have already made alternative arrangements with affected buyers.

key_points.point: Ownership and usage controls are both needed to keep road congestion in check, and ERP 2.0 and other usage tools allow usage policies to be sharpened.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: we will always need a balance of both ownership as well as usage controls

key_points.point: The ministry is watching EV adoption closely and the trend is positive.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: We are watching the adoption of EVs very closely.

left_open: Whether any studies were conducted on the impact of the revised PARF rebate schedule on car depreciation rates and new car demand, and whether those findings can be shared.
Whether transitional measures were considered for car buyers who planned purchases based on the previous depreciation framework.
supplementary: Whether the PARF change signals a shift from ownership to usage pricing, and whether it aims to speed up EV adoption.
